problem_summary.summary: Move from the upper-left to the lower-right of a non-negative grid using only right and down moves, minimizing the sum of visited cells.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an m by n integer grid. Return the smallest sum along a valid path, including both endpoints.

brute_force.explanation: Recursively try moving right and down from each cell, returning the cell value plus the cheaper valid continuation. At the last row or column there is only one possible direction.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every legal path from a cell starts with one of its allowed moves. Taking the minimum of the recursively computed costs therefore yields the best path from that cell.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(2^(m+n)) as a simple upper bound on the branching recursion, where m and n are grid dimensions.

optimized.explanation: Process the grid in row-major order using one array. Before updating column j, its value is the best cost from the cell above; after updating column j-1, that entry is the best cost from the left. Combine the smaller available predecessor with the current cell.
optimized.correctness_idea: Any path entering a cell must come from above or from the left. The rolling array retains exactly those predecessor optima, so each update computes the same minimum as a full two-dimensional table.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary space for one grid row of costs.
